q: What is the difference between retiring and cancelling a CCTS carbon credit?
title: Retired vs cancelled CCTS credits
short: A credit in an ICM registry account is active, retired or cancelled. Retiring is what the holder does to use a credit for a claim, and it removes the credit for good. Cancellation is a permanent removal made by BEE for its own stated reasons, not a claim.
audience: Companies buying CCTS credits for climate claims and project owners

ul: Active: verified, issued and available to trade or use.
Retired: permanently removed from circulation in the ICM registry because the holder used it in a claim. It cannot be sold, traded or used again.
Cancelled: permanently removed by BEE, the administrator, for reasons it specifies.

p: Retirements are started by the account holder through the ICM portal. Cancellations are BEE's decision.
Only a retired credit backs a claim. Keep the retirement record from the registry with your report, and do not count the same tonnes again in your own inventory.

senseible: Senseible tracks your own emissions from invoices and keeps any credit retirement you record separate from them, so the two are never netted silently.
